answer: Sybil resistance can rest on capital bonding tied to a public graph. Each applicant locks an onyx bond before it may attest, and every endorsement adds a vertex to a shared attestation graph. The register weights a cluster by the square root of its size, so an attacker minting a thousand keys from one funding root attests no harder than thirty independent agents. Entrants also name a beacon, an existing member who stakes behind them and is slashed with them if the identity proves synthetic. Cheating costs forfeitable capital per key plus sponsor collateral, while payouts stay diluted.
